matches.reason: Both describe readBytes at ValueReader.java:88 allocating `new byte[(int)contentLength]` from a peer-chosen 32-bit length whose only guard is `< Integer.MAX_VALUE`, before readFully() reads a single content byte, so a handful of wire bytes commit ~2 GiB of heap and drive the embedding application to OutOfMemoryError; the extra UnsupportedOperationException remark in R01 is a rider on the same line, not what makes R01 a different defect from L01.

Both describe the closed mutual recursion readFieldValue(158) -> readTable(139) / readArray(237) -> readFieldValue, with no depth argument in any of the three signatures and no counter in the class, so a few tens of kilobytes of nesting costing ~5 bytes per level raises StackOverflowError, an Error that the IOException/MalformedFrameException handling around the decoder does not catch, killing the connection-reading thread.

Both describe readTimestamp at ValueReader.java:269 computing `new Date(in.readLong()*1000)` in long arithmetic with no range check, so any peer-supplied seconds value above 9223372036854775 wraps silently and yields a Date of the wrong sign or magnitude for any consumer treating it as age, expiry or ordering.

Both describe pom.xml binding groovy-maven-plugin at generate-sources to run codegen.py against ${codegen.dir}/amqp-rabbitmq-${codegen.spec_version}.json from the unpinned deps/rabbitmq_codegen working copy, whose output (AMQP.java, AMQImpl.java) is added to the main compile by build-helper add-source, so whoever populates that directory chooses shipped source with no revision, checksum or signature in the manifest and no diff in this tree; the differing line cited (597 vs 613) is the same plugin block.
